stories.delivered_paragraph: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said the company has never backed a ban on open-weight AI models, pushing back against industry claims that it favors broad restrictions. stories.delivered_paragraph: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said his company is not seeking a ban on downloadable, modifiable open-weight AI models after criticism from other technology companies. Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta and Palantir joined a letter warning policymakers against premature restrictions, while Anthropic did not sign it. The dispute highlights a widening divide between companies selling proprietary systems, including Anthropic’s Claude, and supporters of more freely distributed models.

stories.delivered_paragraph: X has begun rolling out X Money to U.S. Premium and Premium Plus subscribers, expanding Elon Musk’s push to turn the social platform into an “everything app.” The service offers a digital wallet, peer-to-peer transfers, Apple Wallet support and a metal Visa card; it advertises yields of up to 6% APY for eligible users. The broader release follows an invite-only test and will intensify scrutiny of consumer and security safeguards around X’s financial products.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Seattle police now believe at least three people fired guns during the shooting at the Bite of Seattle festival near the Space Needle, revising their initial assessment of two shooters. Three people were killed and at least four injured, including a two-year-old; one suspected shooter died at the scene, a 15-year-old was detained, and another suspect is being sought. The revised account widens the investigation into violence at one of the city’s busiest tourist events.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Small businesses have filed new lawsuits to block the Trump administration’s latest import tariffs, imposed under Section 301 after temporary Section 122 levies expired. The measures generally set duties of 10% or 12.5% on imports from more than 60 economies that Washington says did not sufficiently block forced-labor goods. The cases bring another court test for the administration’s trade strategy after earlier tariff programs were rejected or legally questioned.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A federal magistrate judge ruled that Donald Trump’s trust must provide the BBC with some business financial records as the network defends against Trump’s $10 billion defamation lawsuit. Judge Enjoliqué Aytch Lett granted part of the BBC’s request to compel documents but narrowed the subpoena’s scope. The records could be relevant to arguments over damages, while the limits reduce how much of Trump’s business information the broadcaster can obtain before trial.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Senior U.S. officials believe economic pressure on Iran may ultimately damage its government more than the recent bombing campaign, citing signs of a worsening domestic crisis that includes gasoline shortages. President Trump paused strikes after 13 consecutive days and said Tehran sought talks, a claim Iran denied. Mediators including Oman, Qatar and Pakistan are trying to turn the pause into a durable ceasefire, with Strait of Hormuz traffic among the issues under discussion.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Shots were fired at the U.S. consulate in Toronto for the second time this year, and the suspect remains at large after police pursued a vehicle in a high-speed chase. The incident follows a similar attack in June, when three people were arrested. Repeated targeting of the consulate raises pressure on Canadian authorities to identify whether the attacks are connected and to strengthen security around the diplomatic site.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A Los Angeles judge ruled that musician D4vd, 21, must stand trial over the death of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez after a five-day preliminary hearing featuring testimony from a dozen witnesses. Prosecutors allege he stabbed and dismembered the girl after years of sexual abuse; he has pleaded not guilty. Her remains were found last September in a Tesla registered to his address, and arraignment is set for Aug. 31.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Major League Baseball’s trade market remains largely stalled with the Aug. 3 deadline a week away, as all but eight teams sit within four games of a playoff position. That parity has left clubs reluctant to decide whether to buy or sell, despite speculation around stars such as Detroit’s Tarik Skubal. The next several games may determine which contenders make aggressive moves and whether available talent actually reaches the market.

stories.delivered_paragraph: South Korea’s Kospi and the Nasdaq 100 have become more tightly linked as AI spending ties U.S. technology companies to Korean memory-chip makers, with their 60-day correlation reaching about 0.50, the highest since 2021. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix account for more than half the Kospi, while data centers now use more than half of global DRAM demand. That concentration means a Wall Street tech downturn can increasingly reverberate through Korean equities.

stories.delivered_paragraph: SK Hynix shares fell 10% in Seoul on Tuesday as a broader semiconductor selloff extended after another weak Wall Street session. The drop underscores how exposed Korean chip makers have become to swings in global technology sentiment, particularly around AI investment and demand for memory used in data centers. With Samsung and SK Hynix carrying outsized weight in Korean markets, the rout can also amplify pressure on the broader Kospi.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Investors are scrutinizing reports that Nvidia could backstop an OpenAI data-center lease, an arrangement that would be the largest of its kind, amid warnings that it resembles a tech-bubble financing practice. The concern is that a chip supplier could indirectly support the infrastructure spending that helps drive demand for its own products. Any deal would therefore add to questions about how independently sustainable the AI industry’s rapid data-center buildout is.
